title: 3 ways to prep for your next big race with Search
gist: Google is merchandising AI Mode in Search through a consumer running-prep use case, revealing three commercial hooks: the Canvas planning tool inside AI Mode, an opt-in YouTube Music account connection that lets Search generate playlists, and a Shopping Graph of over 60 billion product listings powering constraint-based product discovery with local availability. The underlying demand signal is that running-related queries like "run club" and "how to train for a marathon" have hit all-time highs this year.

insights.claim: Google reports that running-related search queries including "run club," "how to choose running shoes," and "how to train for a marathon" have reached all-time highs in 2026, framed as part of a broader consumer impulse to unplug from screens.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: First-party query data is a leading indicator for running footwear, apparel, hydration and race-entry demand; a category-wide all-time high in intent queries supports revenue expectations at running-exposed brands and specialty retail.
insights.quote: Searches like “run club,” “how to choose running shoes,” and “how to train for a marathon” have reached all-time highs this year.
insights.locator: As people look for ways to unplug

insights.claim: The stated driver of the running surge is people looking for ways to unplug and 'touch grass,' implying that screen fatigue is itself becoming a demand generator for offline physical-activity categories.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: A digital-fatigue-driven fitness cycle favors physical-goods and experience businesses (races, clubs, gear) over screen-based fitness subscriptions, while the platform still monetizes the planning layer.
insights.locator: As people look for ways to unplug

insights.claim: Google is positioning AI Mode in Search as a multi-week personal planning engine, with a Canvas tool accessed from a plus (+) menu that builds structured training schedules including cross-training and strength-building recommendations tailored to a user's stated pace target, local neighborhood routes and current weekly mileage.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Search moving from ten blue links to persistent generated artifacts encroaches directly on standalone coaching and training-plan apps; watch for engagement shifting away from vertical fitness software.
insights.locator: 1. Create a training plan that’s specific

insights.claim: The example prompt Google chose to showcase bundles a pace goal, a named race, a specific city neighborhood and current training volume into a single query, signaling that the product is optimized for long, highly-parameterized natural-language inputs rather than short keyword searches.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Longer, richer queries mean more tokens and more context per search — an inference cost story for Google, and a higher-intent ad surface where sponsored gear and race placements can be targeted far more precisely.
insights.quote: Help me make a sub 4.5hr training plan for the Texas Marathon with different routes I can run around Montrose. I'm currently running 4x a week with my longest run typically being 7-9 miles.
insights.locator: Try asking, “Help me make a sub 4.5hr

insights.claim: Even inside an AI-generated plan, Google explicitly preserves a path to 'sites and creators across the web,' indicating a deliberate product stance of keeping publisher and creator traffic visible within generative answers.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Relevant to the publisher-traffic debate and regulatory scrutiny of AI answers cannibalizing referrals; Google is building an on-record case that AI Mode still distributes clicks.
insights.quote: You can also discover fresh perspectives from sites and creators across the web.
insights.locator: Select the Canvas tool from the plus

insights.claim: Search now supports an opt-in connection to a user's YouTube Music account so that AI Mode can generate personalized playlists built around that user's favorite artists, extending Search's reach into first-party media consumption data.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Account-linking across Google properties is the durable moat: each connection deepens personalization that standalone chatbots cannot replicate, and raises switching costs alongside privacy and antitrust attention.
insights.quote: If you choose to connect your YouTube Music account with Search, you can ask AI Mode to help create a custom playlist for your run
insights.locator: 2. Fuel your run with custom playlists

insights.claim: The article argues mental endurance matters as much as physical endurance in long-distance training, using boredom management as the justification for embedding a music product inside a training workflow.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Shows the bundling playbook: a utility use case is used to pull users into a subscription media service, a template likely repeated across Google's other properties.
insights.locator: As many runners are well aware

insights.claim: Google states its Shopping Graph contains over 60 billion product listings, which it uses to return tailored recommendations, side-by-side comparisons of in-stock options and local availability inside Search.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: A 60-billion-listing inventory graph with real-time stock and local availability is the asset most directly competitive with Amazon's catalog and the clearest near-term monetization path for AI Mode.
insights.quote: Using Google’s Shopping Graph of over 60 billion product listings
insights.locator: 3. Discover the right gear to keep moving

insights.claim: Product discovery is being reframed around user constraints rather than brand keywords, with examples like road shoes for wide feet, lightweight hydration vests under $80, and anti-chafing apparel.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Constraint-based retrieval weakens brand-keyword bidding as the primary ad mechanic and advantages merchants with rich structured attribute feeds; SEO and retail media budgets have to re-plumb toward attributes.

insights.claim: Surfacing local in-stock availability inside an AI answer converts a generative search into an offline purchase trigger, linking the AI layer to physical retail footfall.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Local-inventory integration is a measurable bridge from AI queries to brick-and-mortar sales, a differentiator against pure-play online marketplaces and a reason retailers keep feeding Google inventory data.
insights.locator: Search can show you tailored recommendations

insights.claim: The post ships with multiple machine-generated summary variants and an audio narration, each labeled 'generated by Google AI' and 'experimental,' showing Google applying AI content repackaging and disclosure labeling to its own first-party corporate communications.
insights.speaker: Peter Schottenfels
insights.so_what: Normalizing multi-format AI re-rendering of a single source text previews where publishing tooling is heading, and sets a disclosure convention regulators may later codify.
insights.quote: This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental
